items.item: `Sources/Translated/Translated.swift`: `+` on two `TranslatedString` values fills a missing
items.reason: Took the issue's first option: each stored language of the sum is lhs[language] + rhs[language] (subscript with fallbacks); the default stays lhs.default + rhs.default. Remaining edge: a language stored on neither side whose fallback chain reaches a language stored on only one side is resolved through the sum's own chain, which can still differ from reading each side in rare chains (e.g. catalan when one side stores spanish and the other french); closing that fully would mean storing derived entries for many languages in every sum.
isEmpty is now default.isEmpty && every stored value isEmpty. Translated.dictionary went from internal to package so the Translating module can read it (that access change is in commit 58c020d8).

Added Dutch, French, German and Spanish (the languages the package's SinglePlural time units translate): en/of/en-of, et/ou/et-ou, und/oder/und-oder, y/o/y-o. Spanish uses the base forms (no e/u euphony). Also [String].formattedList(separator:) in Translating Dependencies now uses the translated and/or per language instead of hard-coded English.

api_changes: Behaviour: TranslatedString(.and/.or/.andOr) and formattedList now give Dutch/French/German/Spanish words; previously English for every language.
notes: No uses of formattedList or the [String].Separator joins outside swift-translating. Tests: Translated Tests.swift (Concatenation), Single Plural Tests/SinglePlural Tests.swift (was an empty file holding only 'import Foundation', now map/flatMap tests), TranslatedString Tests.swift (separator languages), Translating Dependencies Tests/Translating Tests.swift (Emptiness; adds import Translating).
